claims.text: The governing measurement of this trip is the GPS trace, not the rounded trip-record copy. POL-RD-01 makes gps_trace.trace_distance_km the field the threshold test runs on, and it records 23.79 km; trip_record.actual_distance_km of 23.8 km is a rounded convenience copy that may not be cited for the threshold test. Against the booked optimal of 18.3 km, the excess actually driven is 5.49 km.

Both limbs of the establishment test in POL-RD-01 pass and pass comfortably. The excess is 30.0% of the optimal route, above the 20% limb, and 5.49 km in absolute terms, above the 0.8 km limb. A route deviation is therefore ESTABLISHED on this trip's own telemetry.

The trace is clean and no gap-handling discount applies. It carries 187 fixes at a 10 second sample interval across the whole 31 minute trip, 100.0% coverage, an empty gaps array and a max_gap_sec of 0.0. None of limbs (a) to (c) of POL-RD-07 is met, so the deviation stands on the trace alone and the corroboration requirement in POL-RD-07(ii) is not engaged, nor is the escalation in POL-RD-10(3).

The rider has discharged the initial burden under POL-RD-08. Limb (a): the trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown all carry trip identifier TRP-02856, and the trip_record start time of 15:32:19 matches the trace's first fix at 15:32:19. Limb (b): an excess of 5.49 km and 30.0%, measured from a trace that is unimpaired on any limb of POL-RD-07. The burden has shifted to the driver to point to a specific artifact and a specific clause.

The driver's only excuse is the IMM instruction, and the trace destroys it. The rider's message does name a resolved waypoint, but the nearest the vehicle ever came to the IMM waypoint was 3,088.34 metres, at fix index 90 at 15:47:19. Under POL-RD-04 the corroboration test is that the vehicle passes within 200 m of the requested waypoint or travels the requested road; it did neither, and the derived waypoint_approach block records within_threshold as false. Under POL-RD-14 the instruction therefore did not cause the measured excess: POL-RD-04 does not apply, no distance is excluded, and the deviation is decided under POL-RD-01 and POL-RD-02 on the trace as measured.

The driver's one-word reply 'ok' does not rescue the excuse. POL-RD-04 corroboration is geographic, not conversational: the clause requires that the gps_trace show the vehicle within 200 m of the waypoint, and the chat log is the very artifact that supplies the waypoint_hint the test is run against. A message that says 'ok' to a stop the vehicle never approached is a reply to a request, not evidence that the request was performed.

This is not the contradiction POL-RD-10(7) describes, and the case does not escalate on it. A request that was made and a route that did not follow it are consistent facts, not mutually contradictory evidence of comparable strength. POL-RD-14 states that the driver's reliance on the uncorroborated request is an assertion that fails on the trace, and that POL-RD-10(7) is confined to the partly corroborated case, which this is not.

No external traffic cause is available to the driver on this record. The bundle contains no traffic advisory for this trip: EV-ADVIS-02856-01 is admissibility MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0 and no payload, the artifact being minted only so the absence can be cited. I disclose that weight expressly, and cite the artifact for its absence. Because no advisory covers the trip window, the POL-RD-03 comparison cannot be run and any traffic assertion would carry no weight under POL-RD-08. I note that the driver's counterparty statement asserts a rider instruction, not a traffic cause, so nothing turns on POL-RD-13's priority rule here beyond confirming that no exoneration route is open.

There is no endpoint amendment to fall back on. POL-RD-05 requires a non-null pickup_amended_at or dropoff_amended_at and a stored amended_optimal_distance_km, and the trip_record shows amended_optimal_distance_km, amended_optimal_duration_min, pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at all null. The clause cannot be run, no substitute figure may be derived, and the baseline remains the booked optimal of 18.3 km.

Nor is this a pooled trip. The vehicle type on the trip_record is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL, so POL-RD-12 does not apply, no matched-itinerary baseline displaces the booked optimal, and no co-rider collection distance is excluded from the excess.

The fare model on the fare_breakdown is METERED, so the distance-and-time refund route is open and POL-RD-11, which closes that route on upfront-quoted trips, has no application. The rider was billed per kilometre and per minute on a trip that was driven 5.49 km longer than the optimal route.

The POL-RD-02 recomputation is arithmetic and it is not discretionary. ((3.80 + 0.75 x 18.3 + 0.28 x 24.7) x 1.0 surge) + 0.80 platform fee + 0 ERP/tolls + 0 fixed surcharges + 0 waiting time - 0 promo = 25.241. The surge multiplier was read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier, where it is 1.0, and not assumed absent, so no figure is doubled. The fare ledger's own derived money block confirms recomputed_fare of 25.2410.

Charged total was 31.13. Refund = 31.13 - 25.241 = 5.8890 before rounding, rounded up to the nearest SGD 0.05, which is 5.90. That is 18.9% of the charged total, well short of the 90% full-refund share POL-RD-02 sets, and well above the SGD 0.50 de minimis, so the outcome is a PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 5.90 against the rider's contested SGD 8.00.

There is no pass-through line to correct upwards or to double count. The fare_breakdown carries zero ERP and tolls, an empty erp_gantries array, an airport surcharge of 0.0 on a trip that neither originates at nor ends at an airport, and a waiting time fee of 0.0. The off-optimal-route ERP total is 0.00, so POL-RD-09 adds nothing to the POL-RD-02 figure and there is no billing-integrity defect to record.

The rider's own profile does not raise the corroboration bar. rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 1, below the four-claim trigger in POL-RD-08, so no corroboration beyond the gps_trace is required of this claim, and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated of 0 is not reached. I cite that field only for the POL-RD-08 test it names, as POL-GEN-01 requires.

The disputed charge was filed by the rider and the payment status on the fare ledger is CHARGED with refund_issued_sgd of 0.0, so the refund runs to the rider. Under POL-GEN-03 a PARTIAL_REFUND returns part of the contested amount to the filing party and leaves the remainder of the present state standing; the rider should not be left carrying the SGD 5.90 attributable to 5.49 km of driving the optimal route did not require.

Taking the trace figure that governs under POL-RD-01 - gps_trace.trace_distance_km of 23.79 against the booked optimal of 18.3 - the excess is 5.49 km, or 30.0% of the optimal. That clears the establishment gates (0.8 km absolute and 20%) but falls short of BOTH materiality gates set by the same clause, 8.0 km absolute and 50%. This trip is therefore an established but NON-material deviation. Materiality is what opens the driver_profile consultation in POL-RD-06, and it is not reached here, so no material-deviation remedy and no uplift is available to the rider.

The repeat-deviation pattern test is not met and no profile-based amplification is open to the rider. driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against driver_profile.completed_trips_90d of 408 - a rate of 0.00, below the 0.05 threshold, and the raw counter is below the 3 required. No pattern is ESTABLISHED, so neither the FULL_REFUND uplift in POL-RD-06(b) nor the driver-conduct referral in POL-RD-06(c) is available, and the rider's remedy stays on the POL-RD-02 arithmetic. Nor is this a case 'otherwise finely balanced' within POL-RD-06: the trace is unimpaired and unopposed, because the rider's detour request was not corroborated by it. POL-GEN-01 confines this claim to the two fields named above; the lifetime counter prior_deviation_flags is a near-synonym and is not cited, and rating, acceptance_rate, cancellation_rate and active_region are context only.

The rider's IMM request is genuinely on the file and the driver's account is not a bare assertion: chat message MSG-02856-001 was sent BY THE RIDER at 15:33:19, sixty seconds after the meter started, and carries a platform-resolved waypoint_hint for IMM, so limbs (a) to (c) of POL-RD-04 are met. The driver does not, however, claim exoneration under that clause, and candour requires the reason to be stated: the derived waypoint approach places the nearest fix 3088.34 m from IMM, so the 200 m corroboration test in POL-RD-04 fails, and under POL-RD-14 the instruction is taken as not having caused the measured excess and no distance is excluded. The request therefore neither excuses nor aggravates the deviation - it cannot be used to inflate the excess into a material or aggravated one, and the rider's remedy remains the plain POL-RD-01/POL-RD-02 figure on the trace as measured.

The refund on this METERED fare is arithmetic and cannot be inflated. recomputed_fare = (3.80 + 0.75 x 18.3 + 0.28 x 24.7) x 1.0 surge_multiplier read from the FARE_BREAKDOWN + 0.80 platform fee = 25.241; refund = charged_total 31.13 - 25.241 = 5.889, rounded UP to SGD 5.90. That is above the 0.50 de minimis floor, so it is not a NO_ACTION, and it is 18.9% of charged_total, far below the 90% that would convert it into a FULL_REFUND. The driver's whole monetary exposure on this dispute is therefore SGD 5.90 - not the SGD 8.00 contested and not the SGD 31.13 charged.

Nothing is added on top of that figure under POL-RD-09. The fare carries no ERP lines and no airport surcharge: erp_gantries is empty, tolls_erp is 0.00, airport_surcharge is 0.00, and this trip runs from Blk 12 Telok Blangah Cres to Blk 130 Bukit Batok West Ave 6, so it neither originates nor ends at an airport and no surcharge is properly chargeable. There is accordingly no unmatched gantry and no wrongly applied surcharge, no standalone billing-integrity correction arises, and the POL-RD-02 figure of SGD 5.90 is the entirety of what can move on this case.

ruling.explanation:
This is a rider-filed route-deviation dispute over trip TRP-02856 (Blk 12 Telok Blangah Cres to Blk 130 Bukit Batok West Ave 6). Both sides largely agree on the arithmetic, and the arithmetic decides it.

A deviation is ESTABLISHED under POL-RD-01. The governing measurement is the GPS trace (gps_trace.trace_distance_km = 23.79 km), not the rounded trip-record copy of 23.8 km. Against the booked optimal of 18.3 km on EV-TRIP-02856, the excess is 5.49 km, or 30.0% of optimal. Both establishment gates pass (over 0.8 km absolute and over 20%). It does NOT reach materiality: 5.49 km is below the 8.0 km absolute gate and 30.0% is below the 50% gate. Because the deviation is not MATERIAL, the POL-RD-06 driver_profile consultation is not triggered and I accept the driver's point that no FULL_REFUND uplift under POL-RD-06(b) and no driver-conduct referral under POL-RD-06(c) arise. The profile counters confirm this independently: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against 408 completed trips in 90 days, far below the 3-flag and 0.05-rate tests.

The driver's explanation (counterparty statement: 'The rider asked for IMM, it is in the chat', and the chat itself) does not reduce the excess. The rider's message MSG-02856-001 at 15:33:19 does name IMM with a platform-resolved waypoint_hint, and the driver replied 'ok', but POL-RD-04 corroboration is geographic: the trace must pass within 200 m of the waypoint. The derived waypoint approach places the nearest fix 3,088.34 m from IMM (within_threshold false), so the corroboration test fails. Under POL-RD-14 that means the instruction did not cause the measured excess: POL-RD-04 does not apply, no distance is excluded, and the deviation is measured on the trace as it stands. The driver's bare assertion of the request is an assertion that fails on the artifact it rests on. This is also not the mutually contradictory-evidence escalation in POL-RD-10(7): a request made and a route that did not follow it are consistent, and POL-RD-14 confines that trigger to the partly-corroborated case. There is no escalation on this point.

No other exoneration route is open. POL-RD-03 (road closure) needs a traffic advisory: none covers this trip (EV-ADVIS-02856-01 is MISSING, weight 0.0, no payload) and no party asserted a traffic cause, so no traffic excuse is even in play. POL-RD-05 does not run: pickup_amended_at, dropoff_amended_at, amended_optimal_distance_km and amended_optimal_duration_min are all null, so the baseline stays the booked 18.3 km. POL-RD-12 does not run: the vehicle type is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL. POL-RD-11 does not run: the fare model is METERED, not UPFRONT_QUOTE.

The refund is therefore the POL-RD-02 arithmetic on a METERED fare. The surge multiplier was read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier, where it is 1.0, not assumed absent. recomputed_fare = (3.80 + 0.75 x 18.3 + 0.28 x 24.7) x 1.0 + 0.80 platform fee = 24.441 + 0.80 = 25.241. Refund = charged_total 31.13 - 25.241 = 5.889, rounded UP to the nearest SGD 0.05 = SGD 5.90. That is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis (so not NO_ACTION) and 18.9% of the charged total, far below the 90% that would convert it to a FULL_REFUND. The outcome is PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 5.90, not the SGD 8.00 contested and not the SGD 31.13 charged.

Nothing is added under POL-RD-09. The fare carries no ERP lines (erp_gantries empty, tolls_erp 0.00), no airport surcharge (0.00, and the trip neither originates nor ends at an airport), and no waiting-time fee. There is no unmatched gantry and no wrongly applied surcharge, so no billing-integrity finding and no referral arises. Driver compensation under POL-RD-04 does not arise either: the rider was billed 23.8 km against a 23.79 km trace, a shortfall of well under the 1.0 km threshold.

The trace is clean for POL-RD-07 purposes: 187 fixes at a 10-second interval, 100.0% coverage, an empty gaps array and a max_gap_sec of 0.0, so no limb (a) to (c) is met and no corroboration requirement or POL-RD-10(3) escalation is engaged. Trip identifiers match across trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown (TRP-02856), timestamps do not conflict, and no charge line lacks a counterpart. No POL-RD-10 trigger fires. My confidence rests on artifacts all at weight_multiplier 1.0 (EV-GPS-02856, EV-TRIP-02856, EV-FARE-02856, EV-CHAT-02856), so the cap is 1.0; the missing advisory (weight 0.0) carries no deciding fact and does not lower it. The one rider claim citing that absent artifact was discarded at the citation stage for not naming its issue code. My confidence of 0.90 is above the 0.70 floor, so the case does not escalate.

The monetary effect of SGD 5.90 is at or below the POL-GEN-05 execution threshold of SGD 8.00, so this provisional ruling may be executed on issue; either party may appeal under POL-GEN-04.

No traffic advisory is on file. EV-ADVIS-02856-01 is missing (admissibility MISSING, weight_multiplier 0.0), so the POL-RD-03 comparison cannot be run. The driver asserted no traffic cause, so nothing turns on this; and the absence is a gap in the bundle, not an escalation under POL-RD-10(5).

Other routes checked and closed. No endpoint amendment is recorded — amended_optimal_distance_km, amended_optimal_duration_min, pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at are all null — so POL-RD-05 cannot be run and no substitute baseline may be derived. The vehicle type is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL, so POL-RD-12 does not apply. The fare model is METERED, so POL-RD-11 does not close the distance-refund route and POL-RD-02 governs.

Trace integrity. Under POL-RD-07 the trace shows 187 fixes at a 10-second interval, 100.0% coverage, an empty gaps array and a longest gap of 0.0 s. It is not impaired on any of limbs (a) to (c), so no independent corroboration is required and POL-RD-10(3) is not engaged.

The refund arithmetic (POL-RD-02; the surge multiplier is read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier, where it is 1.0, not assumed absent): recomputed_fare = (3.80 + 0.75 x 18.3 + 0.28 x 24.7) x 1.0 + 0.80 platform fee = 25.241. Charged total = 31.13. Refund = 31.13 - 25.241 = 5.889, rounded up to the nearest SGD 0.05, which is 5.90. That is above the 0.50 de-minimis floor and is 18.9% of the charge, so it is a PARTIAL_REFUND and not a full one. POL-RD-09 adds nothing and double-counts nothing: there are no ERP or toll lines, no airport surcharge, no waiting-time fee, and no phantom gantry or wrongly applied surcharge; the bill does not originate at an airport. The rider contested 8.00, but the refund is arithmetic and is not discretionary. No driver compensation arises: the rider was billed 23.8 km against a trace of 23.79 km, so there is no unbilled distance.

Confidence. Every artifact carrying a deciding fact — the trace, trip record, fare ledger and chat log — is at weight_multiplier 1.0, so the cap is 1.0 and my confidence is 0.95. The monetary effect (5.90) is at or below the POL-GEN-05 execution threshold (8.00), so this provisional ruling executes automatically unless either party appeals under POL-GEN-04. One claim in the rider's brief, resting on the absent advisory, was discarded at the citation stage for not naming that artifact's issue code; it is recorded in the audit below.

ruling.explanation:
Both sides agree on the arithmetic and the evidence, and I find the same. This is a route-deviation dispute over a trip from Blk 12 Telok Blangah Cres to Blk 130 Bukit Batok West Ave 6 on 14 Sep 2026, charged SGD 31.13.

Route deviation (POL-RD-01). The governing measurement is the GPS trace, not the rounded trip-record copy: gps_trace.trace_distance_km is 23.79 km against a booked optimal of 18.3 km, an excess of 5.49 km, or 30.0% of optimal. Both establishment gates are cleared (more than 0.8 km and more than 20%), so the deviation is ESTABLISHED. It is not MATERIAL: 5.49 km is below the 8.0 km gate and 30.0% is below the 50% gate. The driver-profile review and the uplift in POL-RD-06 are therefore not engaged, and in any event driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 over 408 completed trips in 90 days — no repeat-deviation pattern exists — so no POL-RD-06(b) uplift and no POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral arise. The driver's own claim to that effect is accepted.

The IMM request. The rider's chat message 'stop at IMM first please' came from the rider one minute after the meter started and carries a platform-resolved waypoint hint, so limbs (a) to (c) of POL-RD-04 are met. The corroboration test, however, fails: the vehicle's nearest fix to IMM was 3,088.34 m, far outside the 200 m threshold, and the trace never travels the requested road. Under POL-RD-14 the request therefore did not cause the measured excess, no distance is excluded, and the route stands as measured. The driver's one-word 'ok' is a reply, not geographic corroboration. This is not the contradiction POL-RD-10(7) describes — a request made and a route not followed are consistent facts — so it does not escalate. No traffic advisory covers this trip (the advisory artifact is MISSING at weight 0.0), so POL-RD-03 yields no exoneration, and none was asserted. POL-RD-05 does not apply (no endpoint amendment; the amended fields are all null) and POL-RD-12 does not apply (vehicle type RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL).

Refund (POL-RD-02). The fare is METERED, so POL-RD-02 governs and POL-RD-11 does not. recomputed_fare = ((3.80 + 0.75 x 18.3 + 0.28 x 24.7) x 1.0 surge) + 0.80 platform fee = 25.241, the surge multiplier having been read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier where it is 1.0. charged_total was 31.13, so the refund is 31.13 - 25.241 = 5.889, rounded UP to SGD 5.90. That is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis and is 18.9% of the charge, far below the 90% that would convert it to a full refund. The outcome is a PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 5.90 to the rider.

ERP and surcharges (POL-RD-09). There are no ERP lines and no airport surcharge on this trip, which neither originates nor ends at an airport, so POL-RD-09 adds nothing to the POL-RD-02 figure and no billing-integrity referral arises.

Escalation (POL-RD-10). No trigger fired. The trace is unimpaired under POL-RD-07(a)–(c) — 187 fixes at a 10-second interval, 100% coverage, no gaps, max gap 0.0 s, max jump well within 500 m — so no independent-corroboration requirement and no POL-RD-10(3) escalation apply. Trip identifiers and pickup timestamps agree across the trip record, trace and fare ledger; no exculpatory clause was invoked against a missing artifact; and no charge line lacks a counterpart. Confidence is well above the 0.70 floor.

Discarded evidence. The referee discarded the rider's traffic-advisory claim because it cited the missing advisory at weight 0.0 without naming its issue code, MISSING_ARTIFACT. The driver's profile claim mentions context-only fields (rating, acceptance_rate, cancellation_rate, active_region, prior_deviation_flags) but expressly disclaims them and rests only on the two fields POL-RD-06 and POL-GEN-01 permit, so it stands. The rider's profile claim likewise cites only the two citable counters, whose values (1 claim, 0 substantiated) are below the POL-RD-08 trigger, so no extra corroboration was required.

The monetary effect, SGD 5.90, does not exceed the POL-GEN-05 execution threshold of SGD 8.00, so this provisional ruling executes automatically, subject to the appeal route under POL-GEN-04.

ledger.claim: The governing measurement of this trip is the GPS trace, not the rounded trip-record copy. POL-RD-01 makes gps_trace.trace_distance_km the field the threshold test runs on, and it records 23.79 km; trip_record.actual_distance_km of 23.8 km is a rounded convenience copy that may not be cited for the threshold test. Against the booked optimal of 18.3 km, the excess actually driven is 5.49 km.

Both limbs of the establishment test in POL-RD-01 pass and pass comfortably. The excess is 30.0% of the optimal route, above the 20% limb, and 5.49 km in absolute terms, above the 0.8 km limb. A route deviation is therefore ESTABLISHED on this trip's own telemetry.

The trace is clean and no gap-handling discount applies. It carries 187 fixes at a 10 second sample interval across the whole 31 minute trip, 100.0% coverage, an empty gaps array and a max_gap_sec of 0.0. None of limbs (a) to (c) of POL-RD-07 is met, so the deviation stands on the trace alone and the corroboration requirement in POL-RD-07(ii) is not engaged, nor is the escalation in POL-RD-10(3).

The rider has discharged the initial burden under POL-RD-08. Limb (a): the trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown all carry trip identifier TRP-02856, and the trip_record start time of 15:32:19 matches the trace's first fix at 15:32:19. Limb (b): an excess of 5.49 km and 30.0%, measured from a trace that is unimpaired on any limb of POL-RD-07. The burden has shifted to the driver to point to a specific artifact and a specific clause.

The driver's only excuse is the IMM instruction, and the trace destroys it. The rider's message does name a resolved waypoint, but the nearest the vehicle ever came to the IMM waypoint was 3,088.34 metres, at fix index 90 at 15:47:19. Under POL-RD-04 the corroboration test is that the vehicle passes within 200 m of the requested waypoint or travels the requested road; it did neither, and the derived waypoint_approach block records within_threshold as false. Under POL-RD-14 the instruction therefore did not cause the measured excess: POL-RD-04 does not apply, no distance is excluded, and the deviation is decided under POL-RD-01 and POL-RD-02 on the trace as measured.

The driver's one-word reply 'ok' does not rescue the excuse. POL-RD-04 corroboration is geographic, not conversational: the clause requires that the gps_trace show the vehicle within 200 m of the waypoint, and the chat log is the very artifact that supplies the waypoint_hint the test is run against. A message that says 'ok' to a stop the vehicle never approached is a reply to a request, not evidence that the request was performed.

This is not the contradiction POL-RD-10(7) describes, and the case does not escalate on it. A request that was made and a route that did not follow it are consistent facts, not mutually contradictory evidence of comparable strength. POL-RD-14 states that the driver's reliance on the uncorroborated request is an assertion that fails on the trace, and that POL-RD-10(7) is confined to the partly corroborated case, which this is not.

No external traffic cause is available to the driver on this record. The bundle contains no traffic advisory for this trip: EV-ADVIS-02856-01 is admissibility MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0 and no payload, the artifact being minted only so the absence can be cited. I disclose that weight expressly, and cite the artifact for its absence. Because no advisory covers the trip window, the POL-RD-03 comparison cannot be run and any traffic assertion would carry no weight under POL-RD-08. I note that the driver's counterparty statement asserts a rider instruction, not a traffic cause, so nothing turns on POL-RD-13's priority rule here beyond confirming that no exoneration route is open.

ledger.claim: There is no endpoint amendment to fall back on. POL-RD-05 requires a non-null pickup_amended_at or dropoff_amended_at and a stored amended_optimal_distance_km, and the trip_record shows amended_optimal_distance_km, amended_optimal_duration_min, pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at all null. The clause cannot be run, no substitute figure may be derived, and the baseline remains the booked optimal of 18.3 km.

Nor is this a pooled trip. The vehicle type on the trip_record is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL, so POL-RD-12 does not apply, no matched-itinerary baseline displaces the booked optimal, and no co-rider collection distance is excluded from the excess.

The fare model on the fare_breakdown is METERED, so the distance-and-time refund route is open and POL-RD-11, which closes that route on upfront-quoted trips, has no application. The rider was billed per kilometre and per minute on a trip that was driven 5.49 km longer than the optimal route.

The POL-RD-02 recomputation is arithmetic and it is not discretionary. ((3.80 + 0.75 x 18.3 + 0.28 x 24.7) x 1.0 surge) + 0.80 platform fee + 0 ERP/tolls + 0 fixed surcharges + 0 waiting time - 0 promo = 25.241. The surge multiplier was read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier, where it is 1.0, and not assumed absent, so no figure is doubled. The fare ledger's own derived money block confirms recomputed_fare of 25.2410.

Charged total was 31.13. Refund = 31.13 - 25.241 = 5.8890 before rounding, rounded up to the nearest SGD 0.05, which is 5.90. That is 18.9% of the charged total, well short of the 90% full-refund share POL-RD-02 sets, and well above the SGD 0.50 de minimis, so the outcome is a PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 5.90 against the rider's contested SGD 8.00.

There is no pass-through line to correct upwards or to double count. The fare_breakdown carries zero ERP and tolls, an empty erp_gantries array, an airport surcharge of 0.0 on a trip that neither originates at nor ends at an airport, and a waiting time fee of 0.0. The off-optimal-route ERP total is 0.00, so POL-RD-09 adds nothing to the POL-RD-02 figure and there is no billing-integrity defect to record.

The rider's own profile does not raise the corroboration bar. rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 1, below the four-claim trigger in POL-RD-08, so no corroboration beyond the gps_trace is required of this claim, and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated of 0 is not reached. I cite that field only for the POL-RD-08 test it names, as POL-GEN-01 requires.

The disputed charge was filed by the rider and the payment status on the fare ledger is CHARGED with refund_issued_sgd of 0.0, so the refund runs to the rider. Under POL-GEN-03 a PARTIAL_REFUND returns part of the contested amount to the filing party and leaves the remainder of the present state standing; the rider should not be left carrying the SGD 5.90 attributable to 5.49 km of driving the optimal route did not require.

Taking the trace figure that governs under POL-RD-01 - gps_trace.trace_distance_km of 23.79 against the booked optimal of 18.3 - the excess is 5.49 km, or 30.0% of the optimal. That clears the establishment gates (0.8 km absolute and 20%) but falls short of BOTH materiality gates set by the same clause, 8.0 km absolute and 50%. This trip is therefore an established but NON-material deviation. Materiality is what opens the driver_profile consultation in POL-RD-06, and it is not reached here, so no material-deviation remedy and no uplift is available to the rider.

The repeat-deviation pattern test is not met and no profile-based amplification is open to the rider. driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against driver_profile.completed_trips_90d of 408 - a rate of 0.00, below the 0.05 threshold, and the raw counter is below the 3 required. No pattern is ESTABLISHED, so neither the FULL_REFUND uplift in POL-RD-06(b) nor the driver-conduct referral in POL-RD-06(c) is available, and the rider's remedy stays on the POL-RD-02 arithmetic. Nor is this a case 'otherwise finely balanced' within POL-RD-06: the trace is unimpaired and unopposed, because the rider's detour request was not corroborated by it. POL-GEN-01 confines this claim to the two fields named above; the lifetime counter prior_deviation_flags is a near-synonym and is not cited, and rating, acceptance_rate, cancellation_rate and active_region are context only.

ledger.claim: The rider's IMM request is genuinely on the file and the driver's account is not a bare assertion: chat message MSG-02856-001 was sent BY THE RIDER at 15:33:19, sixty seconds after the meter started, and carries a platform-resolved waypoint_hint for IMM, so limbs (a) to (c) of POL-RD-04 are met. The driver does not, however, claim exoneration under that clause, and candour requires the reason to be stated: the derived waypoint approach places the nearest fix 3088.34 m from IMM, so the 200 m corroboration test in POL-RD-04 fails, and under POL-RD-14 the instruction is taken as not having caused the measured excess and no distance is excluded. The request therefore neither excuses nor aggravates the deviation - it cannot be used to inflate the excess into a material or aggravated one, and the rider's remedy remains the plain POL-RD-01/POL-RD-02 figure on the trace as measured.

The refund on this METERED fare is arithmetic and cannot be inflated. recomputed_fare = (3.80 + 0.75 x 18.3 + 0.28 x 24.7) x 1.0 surge_multiplier read from the FARE_BREAKDOWN + 0.80 platform fee = 25.241; refund = charged_total 31.13 - 25.241 = 5.889, rounded UP to SGD 5.90. That is above the 0.50 de minimis floor, so it is not a NO_ACTION, and it is 18.9% of charged_total, far below the 90% that would convert it into a FULL_REFUND. The driver's whole monetary exposure on this dispute is therefore SGD 5.90 - not the SGD 8.00 contested and not the SGD 31.13 charged.

Nothing is added on top of that figure under POL-RD-09. The fare carries no ERP lines and no airport surcharge: erp_gantries is empty, tolls_erp is 0.00, airport_surcharge is 0.00, and this trip runs from Blk 12 Telok Blangah Cres to Blk 130 Bukit Batok West Ave 6, so it neither originates nor ends at an airport and no surcharge is properly chargeable. There is accordingly no unmatched gantry and no wrongly applied surcharge, no standalone billing-integrity correction arises, and the POL-RD-02 figure of SGD 5.90 is the entirety of what can move on this case.
